name: Ciarán Walsh
action: Ciarán sets the soldering iron down on its stand, wipes his hands on a rag, and stands. Into the phone, his voice is flat and unhurried: “Give me a few minutes. I’ll be there.” He ends the call, pockets the phone, pulls the shed door shut behind him, and walks toward the station roof without changing or washing.
reason: Ciarán was mid-solder when his sister called, and he recognized that she rarely called on Saturdays and that her calls usually involved something important. He remembered her last call about the children's play, and then recalled the Tuesday he had seen her car at the station and later learned she had waited an hour hoping he would come out. Though his usual pattern was to let family calls ring and call back later, this time he felt that because she had asked outright, and because he could be there in five minutes, the alternator and even the footbridge step could wait. He decided he did not need to shower since she already knew what he looked like, and that meeting her now was easier than letting it sit, leading him to set down the soldering iron and leave immediately.
